paths.description: Public first-time mobile entry and consent journey; represents global shell, preferences, responsiveness, privacy and startup performance.
Representative video detail/watch template using a known public video; covers metadata, content rendering and crawler parity.
Representative search/listing route; confirms the first-time gate and route-level experience.
Unknown route used to inspect resilient failure-state handling for a first-time visitor.

findings.summary: The mandatory consent surface ignores the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme:dark screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance and file size (96,160 bytes) to the light capture, remaining a bright white full-screen surface even though matchMedia reports dark=true.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply color-scheme: light dark to the consent experience and derive surface, text, border, icon, and link colours from system-aware tokens or light-dark().

findings.summary: A long, full-viewport consent interstitial hides all YouTube content before first use.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots on home, search, watch, and an error route show only the consent document; Reject all and Accept all are below the initial 844px viewport after several paragraphs.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the consent copy to the decision-critical summary in the first viewport, keep Reject all and Accept all equally prominent and immediately reachable, and put details behind an accessible disclosure.

findings.summary: The first-time mobile experience paints too slowly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 4.9s, LCP 6.7s, TBT 256ms and performance 0.59; the independent trace measured LCP 3.94s and 286ms total blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the consent surface’s LCP content, reduce startup JavaScript, defer nonessential work, and shorten critical request chains.

findings.summary: Startup JavaScript blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace recorded five long tasks, including 267ms, with 285.88ms total blocking time; layout observation independently found a 413ms task.
findings.suggestedFix: Break startup work into scheduler-prioritised tasks, defer below-the-fold application boot, and avoid hydrating content hidden by consent.

findings.summary: The consent path ships a disproportionate application payload before the user can access content.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 146 requests and 4,047,594 transferred bytes, including 3,031,432 script bytes. Lighthouse estimated 639KiB unused JavaScript and 153KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a minimal consent entry bundle, split the full YouTube application behind the consent decision, remove duplicate/unused code, and defer media/feed requests.

findings.summary: The consent language control has broken accessible naming.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility 0.85 found the visible “en-GB” button name does not match aria-label “Language: English (United Kingdom)”, and the underlying language select has no label or accessible name.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the language picker one consistent accessible name that includes its visible text, and associate a visible or programmatic label with the select.

findings.summary: Some primary UI text fails minimum colour contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured the Search YouTube text at 3.06:1 (#717171 on #272727), below the required 4.5:1 for 16px normal text; links in text also rely on colour alone.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase foreground contrast to at least 4.5:1 and add a non-colour affordance such as underline for links embedded in prose.

findings.summary: The viewport configuration disables user zoom.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found user-scalable=no / a restrictive maximum-scale in the viewport meta. The focus/target probe also measured several header controls at only 24×24 CSS px.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale restrictions, and enlarge compact controls to a minimum 44×44 target while preserving the visible icon size.

findings.summary: The initial page load logs a failed application request.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured an HTTP 400 from /youtubei/v1/feedback?prettyPrint=false and scored the console-errors audit 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not send feedback until required state exists, validate the payload client-side, and handle expected rejection without emitting a console error.

findings.summary: The page misses platform diagnostics and navigation-restoration opportunities.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript, Inspector issues, and a BFCache failure caused by cache-control:no-store plus an HTTP-only cookie mutation.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish production source maps to authorised diagnostics, resolve Inspector issues, and avoid no-store/cookie mutation on pages that can safely use BFCache.

findings.summary: Non-JavaScript crawlers receive only a small fraction of the visible content.
findings.evidence: Discoverability captures classified both home and watch as JavaScript shells with only 6% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML. The crawler screenshots show skeleton cards rather than the rendered labels and page content.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render meaningful feed and watch-page text, links, headings, and state so non-JavaScript crawlers receive the same core content rather than a skeleton shell.

findings.summary: The security policy has avoidable browser-defense gaps.
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS, nosniff, SAMEORIGIN and Trusted Types, but CSP still permits unsafe-eval/unsafe-inline and Referrer-Policy is absent.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsafe-eval and residual unsafe-inline dependencies from CSP, rely on nonces/strict-dynamic and Trusted Types, and set an explicit strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy.

findings.summary: Core content is not progressively available without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML comparison found only 6% content-word coverage on the watch page; the no-JavaScript screenshot is largely a skeleton despite the server response containing title metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Render the watch title, channel, description, transcript affordance, and useful links in server HTML, then enhance playback and recommendations with JavaScript.

findings.summary: The pre-consent network and script budget is disproportionate to the visible consent task.
findings.evidence: The first-load HAR transferred 4.05MB across 146 requests before content access, including 3.03MB script and 100 XHR/fetch requests. Host classification overstates third parties because m.youtube.com redirects to www.youtube.com, but the total work remains large.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict pre-consent budget, suppress media/feed fetching until needed, and defer low-priority background requests with visibility-aware scheduling.

findings.summary: Several mobile header controls expose undersized touch targets.
findings.evidence: The target probe measured Guide, Search, Settings and icon controls at 24×24 CSS px, below the recommended 44×44 mobile target, although consent decision buttons are 40px high and keyboard focus remains visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep 24px icons but enlarge their interactive hit areas to at least 44×44 CSS px and retain visible focus styles.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is burdened by render-blocking and oversized startup resources.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flagged render-blocking requests with an estimated 210ms saving and a long network dependency tree; HAR transferred 4.05MB over 146 requests before consent completion.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical consent CSS, defer/module-load application scripts after the decision, preload only confirmed LCP resources, and shorten the startup dependency chain.

taskList.title: Create a minimal, immediately actionable and preference-aware consent entry surface
Server-render meaningful home and watch content for non-JavaScript consumers
Fix consent/search accessibility: names, labels, contrast, zoom and target size
Tighten CSP and set an explicit Referrer-Policy
Resolve feedback console failure, Inspector issues, source maps and BFCache blockers
